target_customer: Corporate campuses, townships and residential communities in India that deploy shared bikes and e-bikes, plus individual buyers
problem: Last mile and campus mobility in India lacks affordable, healthy options; shared bicycles and e-bikes can serve closed communities where public bike sharing struggles.
business_model: B2B2C bike and e-bike sharing deployments for enterprises and townships, plus direct bike sales and community advertising

founders.name: Deepak VS
founders.background_notes: Per a 2019 Autocar Pro interview snippet the idea began as a bike pool on the SRM campus; the page itself was not opened, so education is left null.

founders.name: Daksh Shah
founders.background_notes: Titled CTO on the YC page. A 2019 article listing four founders could not be opened (HTTP 403).

competitors.name: Yulu
competitors.what: IoT based bicycle and battery scooter sharing in Bengaluru
competitors.traction_then: Named a front runner in Bangalore in 2018

competitors.name: Bounce
competitors.what: Bike and scooter sharing in Bangalore, formerly bicycle based
competitors.traction_then: Named a front runner in Bangalore in 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware plus IoT, locks and app for bike sharing and e-bike supply in India, but using commodity components.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise campus contracts add some stickiness, but bikes and apps were available to rivals and capital intensity was the main barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; larger operators focused on city scooter sharing while Tilt targeted campuses.

market_need_then: Campuses and townships wanted internal mobility, and pandemic era interest in cycling and fitness rose; Tilt reported serving over 1000 users in three months in 2019 and customers such as Tata Motors and TCS.

identity.voice_and_tone: Community and fitness oriented per company blog

rebrands.why: Company blog says the broader vision prompted the evolution from Pedal to Tilt (seen in a search snippet; the post was not opened)

branding.community_and_virality: No merch or fan evidence found; company runs a Medium blog and app based community of riders.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional B2B2C brand known to enterprise customers; the name is generic and shared with many unrelated companies.

pivots.to: Tilt, shared bikes and e-bikes for enterprises and townships, then direct e-bike sales
pivots.why: Broader vision per company blog; e-bike sales appear in 2025 retail listings

outcome_analysis: Tilt grew from a campus bike pool into a B2B2C shared bike and e-bike provider with named corporate customers, took the standard $125K YC deal in 2021 and shows no later disclosed funding. Retail listings in 2025 show it still selling e-bikes, so it survives but with no sourced evidence of venture scale traction.
notes: tilt.bike fetch was rate limited by the safety check, so the company site was not read. Founding year conflicts: YC says 2016, other coverage 2018. CB Insights lists different founders and a $130K total, treated as unreliable. The $125K is the YC deal, recorded as other because it was reported by YourStory and siliconindia. An undisclosed angel round was mentioned in one search result and is not recorded. Founder education and prior employers not found in opened sources.
